newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: Nicaragua ministers seek cover from corruption probe.
newsitem.headline: Nicaragua ministers seek cover from corruption probe.

text.p: Nicaragua's outgoing Cabinet ministers warned an anti-corruption body on Friday to stop attacking officials until charges against them have been proven.
The warning comes amid a series of budding corruption scandals involving government officials being investigated by the Comptroller's Office.

"Serious charges of corruption against government officials must not be launched through public opinion, when the investigations still have not been duly completed, or when those alleged to be involved have not had a chance to defend themselves," a news release by the Cabinet said.
When President Violeta Chamorro came to power in 1990 after her surprise election upset of former Sandinista President Daniel Ortega, she promised a "revolution of honesty."
Chamorro and her ministers will give way to President-elect Arnoldo Aleman and his Cabinet on Jan. 10.
While no corruption charges have touched Chamorro, more than 50 government officials in her administration have been investigated by the comptroller, Augustin Jarquin.
The Comptroller's Office does not have the power to jail corrupt officials but passes the results of its investigations to the judicial system for prosecution.
It is presently auditing top officials in the Health and Transportation ministries, the Central Bank, the Social Security Institute, the National Development Bank and the National Assembly.
All the investigations have been widely publicised, but no one has been convicted yet, prompting government officials to protest through the media.
